title: GovBills role-based video manual
notice: Walkthroughs with AI-generated English narration and captions, using current demo screens, not recordings of live approvals or bank transfers. Reference screens are captured with a demo administrator; your menus and available actions depend on your assigned roles and ministry.

roles.title: Invoice clerk
roles.summary: Receive utility records, check extracted details and prepare a controlled batch.
roles.handoff: Submit a reconciled batch to the independent verification and approval team.

chapters.title: Start with My Work
chapters.instruction: Open My Work to see assigned tasks, returned work and overdue items. Check your ministry and utility provider. My Space stores personal shortcuts; it does not create another copy of an invoice or task.
chapters.action: My Work → tasks and overdue work

chapters.title: Upload records once
chapters.instruction: Use Upload Utility Records for files, a folder or ZIP. Confirm the selection before processing. Authorised mailbox arrivals also enter staged review when configured. Reuse the provider template, check extracted details and ask the unit administrator to resolve missing accounts.
chapters.action: Upload Utility Records → review extracted details

chapters.title: Prepare one provider batch
chapters.instruction: Start batch preparation with one ministry, provider and currency. Select existing detected invoices rather than uploading them again. Check dates, totals, surcharges and source documents. Missing or conflicting records need correction, not another invoice entry.

chapters.title: Resolve blockers and hand over
chapters.instruction: Read the batch readiness panel and follow links to blocking invoices. Provider-list reconciliation and supporting evidence are required. Submit only when the whole batch is ready. Submission requests independent approval; it does not approve invoices or release money.

roles.title: Verifier
roles.summary: Check the complete batch and its invoice evidence before approval.
roles.handoff: Pass the checked batch to the next approval role, or return it with a clear reason.

chapters.title: Find your assigned review
chapters.instruction: Start in My Work or Approvals and open a batch assigned to your workflow role. Check the ministry, utility provider, invoice count and amount. Only work within your authorised scope; another ministry's records are not part of your queue.
chapters.action: My Work or Approvals → assigned batch

chapters.title: Review the entire batch
chapters.instruction: Approval work is batch-based. Open the batch review and compare every member with its source evidence. Check account allocation, bill period, due dates, totals and surcharge handling. A summary count alone is not evidence that the invoice details are correct.

chapters.title: Handle a mismatch explicitly
chapters.instruction: Use the batch issues and invoice links to investigate missing documents or reconciliation mismatches. Record a useful explanation when returning work. Do not re-enter the invoice or edit an approved snapshot to make a mismatch disappear; use the controlled correction route.

chapters.title: Record the authorised decision
chapters.instruction: Read the proposed batch decision and confirm its scope before submitting. Sign only if your configured step requires it. You must not decide an invoice you recorded or submitted, and independent workflow steps cannot be combined into one person's approval.
chapters.action: Batch review → decision → next workflow role

roles.title: Approver
roles.summary: Make an independent batch decision supported by reconciliation and evidence.
roles.handoff: Send fully approved batches to finance without bypassing payment controls.

chapters.title: Open the batch approval queue
chapters.instruction: Open Approvals and select an assigned batch. Review its ministry, provider, invoice count, amount and next deadline. The decision applies to the batch, not an isolated invoice selected outside the approval package.

chapters.title: Check evidence and exceptions
chapters.instruction: Inspect the batch invoices, reconciliation evidence, authorised adjustments and any outstanding dispute. Open supporting invoice records when needed. A readiness check helps navigation but never replaces your independent review or the server's final validation.

chapters.title: Decide and sign when required
chapters.instruction: Choose the appropriate batch decision and record a clear comment. Required signing steps use your own signing credential. Never use another officer's account or sign a step you are not eligible to decide. Returned work must follow correction and reapproval controls.
chapters.action: Batch review → decision and required signature

chapters.title: Inspect the handoff and record
chapters.instruction: Check the batch journey and history to see the next responsible role. Review the operational stamped invoice copy where available. A stamp records captured review and approval evidence; missing settlement information remains missing until finance records it. Approval is not payment.
chapters.action: Batch → journey, history and invoice copy

roles.title: Finance officer
roles.summary: Reconcile provider lists, group approved batches and track settlement outcomes.
roles.handoff: Request independent payment authorisation, then track bank and provider handoffs.

chapters.title: Match the provider listing
chapters.instruction: Open Provider reconciliation and import the provider's pending-invoice XLS or CSV. Match the account, invoice reference, currency and amount. Investigate Unsorted mismatches with a responsible owner. Reconciliation is required before both approval and settlement.

chapters.title: Group eligible approved batches
chapters.instruction: Open Settlements and group eligible approved batches for one provider and currency, respecting ministry boundaries. Original batch identities and audit histories remain intact. Review the payable total and authorised adjustments; no partial or unreconciled release should be disguised as a complete batch.

chapters.title: Prepare the bank handoff
chapters.instruction: Prepare the settlement instruction and request independent authorisation. The bank handoff must retain invoice-level entries and references. The final bank layout still needs the supplied bank specification; a demonstration export must not be treated as a certified payment file.

chapters.title: Confirm and reconcile payment
chapters.instruction: Record the actual bank outcome and inspect Bank reconciliation for matched debits or discrepancies. Track provider settlement advice separately. Creating or sending a file is not confirmed payment. Keep failed or uncertain submissions visible and retain evidence before closing the settlement.

roles.title: Payment authoriser
roles.handoff: Return an authorised instruction to finance; bank execution remains a separate event.

chapters.title: Find payment authorisation work
chapters.instruction: Use My Work and Settlements to find instructions awaiting your authorisation. Confirm that the instruction belongs to your authorised ministry and payment role. Do not create a replacement instruction because the original is waiting for another officer.

chapters.title: Review the instruction package
chapters.instruction: Inspect the provider, currency, member batches, invoice references, total and supporting approval evidence. Confirm reconciliation remains current and review changes or holds. Use the existing invoice and batch records; do not capture their amounts again in a parallel worksheet.

chapters.title: Preserve separation of duties
chapters.instruction: Review the batch history and the people who prepared and approved it. Use your own authorised signing credential only when all checks are satisfied. Missing evidence must be returned for resolution, never bypassed because a due date is close.

chapters.title: Understand what happens next
chapters.instruction: After authorisation, finance handles the bank submission and records the outcome. Authorisation is permission to proceed, not proof that funds moved. Bank reconciliation and provider advice have separate evidence and statuses. Uncertain or failed transfers remain exceptions until investigated.

roles.title: Unit administrator
roles.summary: Maintain ministry account allocation and help staff resolve blocked processing.
roles.handoff: Return corrected master data and assigned exceptions to the responsible processors.

chapters.title: Maintain allocated service accounts
chapters.instruction: Open Service accounts and filter by ministry, provider, service, account status and invoicing status. Confirm the account number, service purpose and responsible owner. Use the existing register; registering another copy of the same provider account is not a correction.

chapters.title: Resolve missing or inactive accounts
chapters.instruction: Register genuinely missing accounts for the correct ministry. Review on-hold, disputed, suspended or decommissioned services before processing resumes. Do not transfer an account or historical invoices between ministries merely because an uploaded document was assigned incorrectly.

chapters.title: Support the processing team
chapters.instruction: Use assigned work and overdue views to find unresolved exceptions. Allocate responsibility and explain what needs correcting. Personal schedules organise work but never approve or pay bills automatically. Reuse the same invoice and preparation records when staff return to the task.
chapters.action: My Work → overdue work and assigned exceptions

chapters.title: Monitor delays fairly
chapters.instruction: Review ministry timeliness and surcharge reports. Distinguish provider issue dates, receipt dates, internal processing delays and payment outcomes before attributing a surcharge. Follow the authorised user and workflow administration routes available to your role; do not grant yourself wider financial access.

roles.title: Auditor
roles.summary: Trace evidence from receipt through approval, settlement and bank matching.
roles.handoff: Report findings through authorised channels without changing financial execution.

chapters.title: Choose the audit scope
chapters.instruction: Select the authorised ministry, provider and reporting period. Drill from summary figures to their underlying records. Keep currencies separate and distinguish operational overdue work from approved payable liabilities. A draft invoice is not automatically an approved debt.

chapters.title: Trace the batch evidence
chapters.instruction: Open a batch and inspect source invoice links, membership, processing owners, decisions and lifecycle history. Settlement grouping must retain the member batches. Compare the operational stamped copy with original documents and signed evidence; a visual stamp is not a substitute for signature verification.

chapters.title: Inspect changes and separation
chapters.instruction: Use the Audit trail to follow who recorded, submitted, reviewed, approved and authorised each stage. Check timestamps, returned work, disputes and authorised adjustments. Post-payment waivers or refunds must preserve the original payment history rather than rewriting it.
chapters.action: Audit trail → events and supporting records

chapters.title: Verify settlement closure
chapters.instruction: Trace the settlement instruction, bank submission reference, actual payment outcome and statement match. Review provider advice and unresolved differences separately. Audit access does not permit you to authorise payments or silently repair the evidence you are inspecting.

roles.title: Viewer
roles.summary: Understand status and reports without performing processing or financial actions.
roles.handoff: Refer questions or exceptions to the responsible assigned team.

chapters.title: Read your authorised overview
chapters.instruction: Start with the Overview for your ministry and role. The provider filter limits the records shown. Summary figures should drill into the matching records. Menus visible in these administrator reference screens may not be available to a read-only viewer.

chapters.title: Understand the batch folders
chapters.instruction: Use Batches to distinguish Preparation, Work in progress, Rejected and Completed. A folder is a navigation view, not a separate copy of the invoices. Open a batch to understand its current status and the team responsible for the next stage.

chapters.title: Read the current stage
chapters.instruction: Inspect the batch journey, available invoice links and history within your permissions. A blocking issue explains why work cannot progress. Ready for approval, approved, authorised and paid are different states; never treat a submitted bank file as proof of payment.

chapters.title: Escalate without changing records
chapters.instruction: Send the batch or invoice reference to the responsible team when you spot a problem. Viewer access does not grant permission to upload, correct, approve, sign or pay records. Ask an administrator for legitimate access changes rather than borrowing another user's account.
chapters.action: Identify responsible team → share record reference

roles.title: System administrator
roles.summary: Configure access, workflows and gateways without bypassing financial governance.
roles.handoff: Provide a controlled environment for ministry staff and independent financial roles.

chapters.title: Check system readiness
chapters.instruction: Open Admin console and review system health and configuration. Confirm the environment is a demonstration or approved live deployment before setup changes. Keep credentials, signing material and integration secrets outside training files and exports. Configuration does not establish that payments or notifications were delivered.

chapters.title: Assign minimum necessary access
chapters.instruction: Use Users and roles to create individual accounts and assign ministry-scoped responsibilities. Set or reset passwords only through authorised controls. Staff must use their own authentication and signing setup. Administrator access is not permission to ignore independent approval and payment duties.
chapters.action: Users and roles → individual scoped access

chapters.title: Configure controlled workflows
chapters.instruction: Maintain workflow policies, required roles, deadlines and signing steps. Ensure eligible independent officers exist for every stage. Test changes using demonstration records. Preserve approval evidence and required revalidation; do not alter policy just to push a blocked live batch through.
chapters.action: Workflow configuration → roles, steps and controls

chapters.title: Configure trusted intake and delivery
chapters.instruction: In Gateway centre, map dedicated incoming mailboxes and exact authorised senders to utility providers. Configure and test outgoing channels separately. Unconfigured Outlook, SMS or bank integrations are not live automation. Keep OCR templates shared by provider and retain audit evidence for administrative changes.
chapters.action: Gateway centre → authorised intake and delivery
